problems.stem: Which combination of factors most distinguishes AI ethics from general engineering ethics?
options: AI is just more complicated than other software.
Scale, encoded decisions in technical choices, multiple invisible stakeholders, and the shift toward generative/autonomous behavior — so ethics cannot be added as a final review step.
AI is fully regulated by law, so ethics is settled.
problems.explanation: The combination of scale, encoded ethical decisions, invisible stakeholders, and generative/autonomous behavior is what makes AI ethics a distinct subject.

problems.stem: A bank deploys an AI loan-decision model trained on past customer data. Who are the stakeholders an ethics review must consider?
options: Only the customers who interact with the deployed system.
The decision-maker (bank), the decision subjects (loan applicants), the data subjects (past customers whose data trained the model), and bystanders (e.g., neighborhoods systematically denied credit).
Only the bank, since they own the system.
problems.explanation: AI systems typically affect four stakeholder groups: decision-maker, decision subject, data subject, and bystanders. A user-only frame misses three of the four.

problems.stem: When does an ethical decision happen in a typical AI project?
options: Only at the deployment phase, when humans review the output.
Only when laws require an ethics review.
At every technical choice that encodes value judgments — selecting the target variable, choosing the training distribution, setting deployment thresholds — not just at a 'review' phase at the end.
Never, because AI systems are objective.
problems.explanation: Technical choices like target variable, data distribution, and threshold are themselves ethical decisions. The model encodes the policy.

problems.stem: What is the most accurate relationship between AI ethics and AI law?
options: Ethics and law are identical; if it is legal it is ethical.

Law encodes some ethical commitments (GDPR, FERPA, EU AI Act) into binding language, but many ethical questions about fairness, power, and long-term effects remain unsettled in law and still require engineering judgment.
Ethics is purely subjective and law is purely objective.
Law is irrelevant to AI ethics.
problems.explanation: Law operationalizes some ethical norms but leaves many open. Compliance is necessary, not sufficient.
